surprises.description: LECO reported $1.221 billion of sales and adjusted EPS of $2.98, above the preview’s $1.17 billion consensus and $2.81 EPS consensus, as well as its own estimates of about $1.188 billion and $2.88. The gaps were meaningful, particularly against the consensus revenue estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 adjusted EPS rose 21% to a record $2.98, with sales up 15% to $1.221 billion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 Consensus”: Net sales $1.17B; adjusted EPS $2.81. The preview’s model estimated total sales of ~$1,188M and adjusted EPS of ~$2.88.

surprises.description: The preview focused on whether volume could take over from decelerating price, but LECO’s 9% volume growth exceeded its 6% price contribution. This was the first quarter in over 2.5 years that volume growth outpaced price.
surprises.fact_evidence: Sales growth was driven by “9% volume growth and 6% price”—the first quarter in over 2.5 years that volume growth outpaced price.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The “central question” was whether “volume growth can take the baton from a decelerating price contribution”; the preview also said price comps harden materially in 2H and asked whether volume was visibly accelerating.

surprises.description: Gross margin fell much more sharply than the preview’s price-cost concerns suggested: it declined 190 basis points, and LECO was still 100 basis points behind its neutral price/cost target year-to-date. Management now expects to close that gap in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross profit margin compressed 190 basis points to 34.8% due to late-quarter price increases and unfavorable mix; the company was 100 basis points behind its neutral price/cost target year-to-date and expects to close the gap in Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said price-cost was “guided to neutral in 2H after -10bp in Q2,” flagged the “LIFO drag,” and called gross-margin direction a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin was slightly below the preview model, and incremental margin was below the preview’s assumed mid-20s level. Year-over-year operating margin still improved, but less than the preview’s modeled margin and incremental leverage implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted operating income margin improved 60 basis points to 18% at a 22% incremental margin.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “~18.3% adj. operating margin” and a “25% incremental margin,” consistent with the “mid-20%” 2H guide.

surprises.description: Americas Welding sales exceeded the preview’s segment estimate, growing 16% rather than the estimated 10.6%. Its 20.1% margin also cleared the preview’s 19–20% 2H range, and management’s Q4 margin outlook is higher still.
surprises.fact_evidence: Americas Welding sales rose 16% to $801 million and adjusted EBIT margin expanded 190 basis points to 20.1%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Americas Welding at “~$765M” and “+10.6%”; it said the 2H margin guide was 19–20%.

surprises.description: Management guided to a 20–21% Americas Welding margin in Q4, above the preview’s 19–20% 2H margin range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided to a 20%-21% Americas Welding margin in Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified the Americas Welding “19–20% 2H guide.”

surprises.description: International Welding sales were materially below the preview’s segment estimate: $227 million versus about $238 million, with growth of just 3% rather than the estimated 8.4%. Its 10.3% margin, however, remained within the preview’s expected 10–11% area.
surprises.fact_evidence: International Welding sales rose only 3% to $227 million, with EBIT margin at 10.3%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated International Welding at “~$238M” and “+8.4%,” and said it was watching for performance “toward 10–11%.”

surprises.description: The Q3 Middle East conflict headwind was smaller than the preview’s stated quarterly $6–7 million headwind. The company still expects a $6–7 million impact in Q4, consistent with the preview’s concern for that quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Q3 impact was approximately $5 million; the expected Q4 impact is $6–7 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged a “$6–7M quarterly Middle East conflict headwind.”

surprises.description: Harris Products Group sales exceeded the preview estimate, reaching $193 million versus about $185 million, but its 17.3% margin fell below the preview’s 18–19% range. The revenue growth was heavily driven by silver-related price increases, while mix and operational inefficiencies weighed on margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: Harris sales jumped 29% to $193 million on approximately 26% higher price, largely due to silver costs; EBIT margin fell 100 basis points to 17.3%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Harris sales of “~$185M” and said to watch for an “18–19%” margin, while warning that metals pass-through could make a revenue beat low quality.

surprises.description: Automation growth and orders were stronger than the preview’s expected high-single- to low-double-digit trajectory: sales grew at a high-teens organic rate, and strong orders pushed backlog to new records.
surprises.fact_evidence: Automation sales reached $232 million on high-teens percent organic growth, and strong orders in automation and equipment pushed backlog to new record levels.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “high-single to low-double-digit trajectory” and said order or pipeline quantification would be upside optionality.

surprises.description: Demand was broader than the preview’s base case required: all five end markets grew, including transportation, which the preview singled out as needing to turn positive in the bull case. U.S. sales grew over 20%, with general fabrication up mid-20s and energy and structural steel up mid-teens.
surprises.fact_evidence: U.S. sales grew over 20% and all five end markets grew; transportation was up low double digits.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case called for “transportation turning positive after Q2’s mid-single-digit decline.”

surprises.description: LECO raised full-year sales-growth guidance to the low-teens range, rather than merely reaffirming the low-double-digit outlook described in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company raised full-year sales growth guidance to the low-teens percent range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said current guidance was “low-double-digit net sales growth” and framed a reaffirmation as the base case, with another raise in the bull case.

surprises.description: The 2026 CapEx plan increased beyond the range in the preview, raising planned investment by roughly $30 million at the midpoint. The added spending is intended to fund capacity and RISE initiatives.
surprises.fact_evidence: 2026 CapEx increased to $140–150 million from an initial $110–130 million to fund capacity and RISE initiatives.
